BL-SETUP-003.story: The platform is split into modules (Core, Auth, Workspaces and the rest) so each feature has its own home and can grow on its own.

BL-CORE-001.story: You can check whether platform services (database, cache, queue) are healthy with one call to /api/health.

BL-CORE-002.story: You install StellarCrew from the command line — a single command creates the first admin and flips the installed flag.

BL-CORE-003A.story: User lives inside the Auth module — other modules consume it as a ready-made port, without reaching into internals.

BL-CORE-003B.story: The install panel talks to the API — status check and form submission through /api/install/status and /api/install.

BL-CORE-003C.story: You install StellarCrew through the browser — a form with real-time validation.

BL-CORE-003C-hotfix.story: The home page / correctly redirects you to the installer until the system has been installed.

BL-CORE-003D-a.story: The installer walks you through 5 steps — admin, branding, logo, first workspace, review.

BL-CORE-006.story: Identifiers and time are typed in one place — less risk of mix-ups at module boundaries.

BL-CORE-007.story: Backend errors land on the frontend in one JSON shape — readable messages instead of raw 500s.

BL-AUTH-001.story: You sign in with e-mail and password — the API returns a JWT valid for one hour.

BL-AUTH-002.story: The frontend remembers your token — every request carries Authorization: Bearer automatically.

BL-AUTH-003.story: The home page is guarded — anonymous visitors go to /login; in the topbar you see yourself and have a Sign out button.

BL-UI-001.story: The sidebar menu assembles from modules — each module contributes its items through MenuContributor, respecting your role.

BL-UI-002.story: The app has a shell: a 240 px sidebar with logo, collapse arrow, sections, footer — with /dashboard, /workspaces and PL/EN labels.

BL-UI-003.story: Below the logo there's a workspace switcher placeholder — first iteration with a single Default workspace.

BL-UI-TOPBAR.story: You get a topbar with a profile menu — sign out, language and theme moved from the sidebar to the top-right corner.

BL-UI-FIX-01.story: Deptrac stays green — the menu DTO respects module boundaries.

BL-UI-004.story: You pin menu items — a star next to each, pinned ones go to the top (max 5), persisted in localStorage.

BL-UI-POLISH-001.story: Unified Button and Input components — primary/secondary/destructive variants, aria-invalid on errors, Design 2.0.

BL-WS-UI-001.story: Workspace dialogs (create, edit, delete) use the unified Button and Input — consistent Design 2.0 look.

BL-UI-POLISH-002.story: Breadcrumbs in the topbar — a Home icon and a chevron-separated path to the current view, driven by usePageBreadcrumbs.

BL-WS-UI-002.story: The delete workspace dialog requires a confirmation checkbox — smaller risk of an accidental click.

BL-UI-STRETCH.story: Content stretches to full width — unified padding, no narrow container from earlier iterations.

BL-UI-POLISH-003.story: Confirm modals are wider (max-w-2xl), the Reactivate CTA is red like Deactivate/Delete, user-management dialogs render via a portal — no more inherited text-align: right from the row actions cell.

BL-UI-POLISH-004.story: Confirm modals keep a stable minimum height on the body text section — a short one-sentence message no longer collapses at the top of the modal.

BL-UI-POLISH-005.story: The audit log view stretches to full width — no more inner max-w-6xl plus double padding (AppLayout `<main>` already uses p-7).

BL-UI-POLISH-006.story: Informational and warning modals (ResetPasswordDialog, UndoConfirmDialog, AuditDetailsDialog) show the icon in the header text color with no colored pill — only Danger/Delete keeps the red circle.

BL-WS-001.story: The workspace domain is in place — Workspace, Member, Invitation; on install a Default workspace owned by the admin is seeded.

BL-WS-002.story: You manage workspaces over the API — create, update, delete (soft), with permission guards.

BL-WS-003.story: You define your own Workspaces — a tiled view at /workspaces, a dialog with name, color and initials, delete with confirmation.

BL-WS-004.story: The frontend remembers which workspace you picked — restores it after refresh and login, clears it on logout.

BL-WS-005.story: A real workspace switcher lives in the sidebar — popover with the list, a Manage link, a tile in collapsed mode.

BL-WS-HOTFIX-001.story: Hotfix: the frontend stopped sending hex colors — later rolled back by HOTFIX-002; we stay on hex.

BL-WS-HOTFIX-002.story: Workspace color is stored as #RRGGBB — validated by regex, any color from the frontend palette allowed.

BL-UM-001.story: Each user has a profile — a dedicated user_management schema, admin profile seeded on install.

BL-UM-002.story: You create users through the API — every creation hits the audit log with after_state (e-mail, super admin flag).

BL-UM-003.story: A super admin adds users via POST /api/user-management/users — DTO with validation (unique e-mail, min 12-char password).

BL-UM-004.story: You list users with filters — by e-mail, workspace, super admin flag, deactivated; with pagination.

BL-UM-005.story: Super admin gets /admin/users — table, filters, Add user modal, sidebar menu item.

BL-UM-006.story: You manage workspace members — assign, change role, remove; an admin must be downgraded before removal.

BL-UM-007.story: Workspace member HTTP endpoints — POST/PATCH/DELETE under /workspace-assignments, 422 when trying to remove the admin.

BL-UM-008.story: A workspace owner manages members in the UI — table, autocomplete to add, role select, delete modal.

BL-UM-009.story: You see your role in every workspace — role pills (owner, admin, member, guest) on tiles, in the switcher and in the profile dropdown.

BL-UM-010.story: User detail at /admin/users/{id} — status, workspace assignments, account section, last 20 audit entries linking to the full log.

BL-UM-011.story: You deactivate and reactivate accounts — confirmation modals, audit log, both actions reversible.

BL-UM-012.story: A super admin resets a user's password — modal with two password fields, audit entry without the password (non-reversible).

BL-UM-013.story: The users table has a row action menu — three options: Details, Deactivate/Reactivate, Reset password.

BL-UM-014.story: Every admin action carries the real actor id to the audit log — no more 500s on deactivate, reactivate, password reset, member role change and member removal.

BL-UM-MEMBERS-LINK.story: The workspace tile now has a Members icon — one click opens `/workspace/{id}/settings/members` where you can add/remove members and change their roles.

BL-UM-VISIBLE-ADMIN-FIX.story: Super admin sees every user in the Add-member autocomplete — the shared-workspace filter no longer applies to admin accounts.

BL-UM-MEMBERS-KEBAB.story: The Remove member action in the workspace members table moved under a kebab menu (consistent with UserTable and the audit table) — no more inline buttons in the actions column.

BL-AUDIT-001.story: Audit schema and audit_log table are in place — actor, action, resource, before/after as JSONB, undo markers, indexes.

BL-AUDIT-002.story: Modules write to the audit — AuditApi::log implements the shared AuditLoggerInterface.

BL-AUDIT-003.story: You search the audit log via API — GET /api/audit/entries with filters (actor, action, resource, date range, reversible, undone), super admin only.

BL-AUDIT-004.story: You undo an audit entry — dispatcher collects Undoer per module, POST /api/audit/entries/{id}/undo returns a new entry id with 404/409/410/422 error mapping.

BL-AUDIT-005.story: There's an /admin/audit view — table with filters (actor autocomplete, action grouped per module, resource, date range) and an Undo button with an effect description.

BL-AUDIT-006.story: The Audit log menu item appears in the sidebar (super admin only).

BL-AUDIT-LOGIN.story: The audit log records successful logins and logouts — with IP, user-agent and account e-mail. Logout now requires a JWT (POST /api/auth/logout with Bearer).

BL-AUDIT-UI-ACTIONS.story: The audit table has an Actions kebab menu — Details opens a modal with the full before/after state and metadata; Undo stays the same (disabled for non-reversible or already undone entries).

BL-AUDIT-WS-CRUD.story: Workspace lifecycle is audited — create, edit (name, icon color, initials) and delete all land in the audit log with state snapshots, each reversible through the dedicated Undoer (restore previous state or revive the deleted workspace).

BL-PLUGIN-ARCH.story: Plugin architecture — modules installed per workspace (not instance-wide), scoped routing, menu, API endpoints and tables. Research in `knowledge/discovery/plugin-architecture.md`, waiting for an ADR.

BL-AUDIT-007.story: You can undo 6 User Management actions: user creation, deactivation and reactivation, member assignment, removal and role change.

BL-INT-FOUNDATION.story: Foundation for atomic integration tests — DAMA DoctrineTestBundle (transaction rollback per test), IntegrationTestCase base class, TracingDomainEventDispatcher for asserting dispatched events, split Test + DataProvider files. Also covers BL-UM-004 follow-up (real-DB ListUsersIntegrationTest). Brief: `knowledge/briefs/1e-integration-tests.md`, 6 decisions pending.

BL-PERM-001.story: Per-module permissions (workspaces.view, workspaces.manage, agents.view, and so on) — UserRole as shorthand for the full set in a workspace.

BL-PERM-002.story: Symfony voters check membership and permission per workspace — replacing the Admin/User flag at the policy boundary.

BL-PERM-003.story: A workspace owner manages member roles and individual permissions in the UI.

BL-AGENTS-001.story: Admin seeds a catalog of predefined agents (Maja, Viktor, Diego and more) from a CLI or panel.

BL-AGENTS-002.story: You copy an agent from the catalog into your own list, or create a custom one from scratch.

BL-AGENTS-003.story: You assign an agent to a workspace or a project — one agent per place (unique scope + scope_id pair).

BL-AGENTS-004.story: You tweak your agent's name, instructions, color and memory without touching the catalog template.

BL-AGENTS-005.story: Each agent carries memory — types conversation / document / embedding / note; memory can be personal or shared.

BL-AGENTS-006.story: Each agent gets its own context strategy — selection rules (RAG top-K, recency, importance) specified per agent.

BL-AGENTS-007.story: Pinned agents live in the sidebar next to the workspace switcher — with a scope badge and a quick jump.

BL-AGUI-001.story: The frontend talks to the Agents and Agent Templates endpoints through a shared API layer with eight typed hooks.

BL-AGUI-002.story: An Agents page at /agents lists your agents as tiles with an empty state and a dedicated Add button — the sidebar entry is now live.

BL-AGUI-003.story: Clicking Add agent opens a choose-path dialog that offers either From template or From scratch.

BL-AGUI-004.story: From template leads to a picker grid of five predefined agents with avatars, role and short description.

BL-AGUI-005.story: Picking a template opens a pre-filled form (name, role, slug + five prompt sections) that creates the agent on submit.

BL-AGUI-006.story: From scratch opens an empty form with the same five prompt sections — you define every section yourself.

BL-AGUI-007.story: Each agent has a read-only overview with metadata, five prompt sections and an activity stub (Coming after CHAT).

BL-AGUI-008.story: Agent settings let you rename, retune the five sections and soft-delete the agent — the list shows a success banner with Undo in the Audit log.

BL-AGAUDIT-001.story: Creating an agent is recorded in the audit log with a full after-state snapshot of every field.

BL-AGAUDIT-002.story: Editing an agent is recorded with before and after snapshots, so the audit log shows exactly what changed.

BL-AGAUDIT-003.story: Soft-deleting an agent is recorded with a before snapshot; repeating the delete stays a no-op and skips the log.

BL-AGAUDIT-004.story: Creating an agent from a template records the full snapshot plus the origin template slug for traceability.

BL-WSUX-001.story: On large screens (≥1280px) the workspace grid shows 4 tiles per row instead of 3 — better use of horizontal space.

BL-WSUX-002.story: Entering a workspace from the list lands you on the workspace Overview page (new URL layer `/workspace/{id}/overview`).

BL-WSUX-003.story: Sidebar reveals a contextual Workspace section (Overview/Projects/Members/Agents/Scheduler/Settings) once you're inside a workspace — unavailable items are greyed out with a milestone note.

BL-WSUX-004.story: Workspace Overview page uses a dashboard layout with 2 widget rows (row 1: 5 widgets, row 2: 3 widgets).

BL-WSUX-005.story: Widget „Active Tasks" shows what's being worked on today + time spent (PROTOTYPE, final after TASKS milestone).

BL-WSUX-006.story: Widget „Active Agents" shows count of active agents + list with current mode per agent (BUILDER/LISTENER/DISCOVERY/IDLE). PROTOTYPE.

BL-WSUX-007.story: Widget „Tasks Progress" shows overall progress + 3 most recent tasks with status and %. PROTOTYPE.

BL-WSUX-008.story: Widget „Milestones" shows active milestone and progress. PROTOTYPE.

BL-WSUX-009.story: Widget „Projects" shows project count + preview tiles (PROTOTYPE, final after PROJECTS milestone).

BL-WSUX-010.story: Widget „Boss Actions" shows what agents are waiting on from boss (Code Review, Tests, ...). PROTOTYPE.

BL-WSUX-011.story: Widget „Last Agents Activity" shows list of completed BLs in format `BL-ID description commit-hash` + status badge (merged/pending/in-progress). PROTOTYPE.

BL-WSUX-012.story: Widget „Workspace Info" shows workspace avatar, description, created-by, created-at, copy-workspace-ID button. PROTOTYPE.

BL-WSUX-TILE-LINK.story: Workspace tile avatar + name + slug + role pill are wrapped in a link that opens `/workspace/:id/overview`. Hover actions (members, edit, delete) stay separate and keep their own targets.

BL-WSUX-PROJ-SHELL.story: Route `/workspace/:id/projects` serves a placeholder page (header + "Coming after PROJECTS milestone" message). Sidebar Workspace section lifts Projects out of the disabled list and makes it an active link. Prepares a landing target for the Project Overviews widget CTA.

BL-WSUX-PROJ-OVERVIEW.story: Workspace Overview gets a third row with a Projects Overview widget: a 4-column grid of 7 faux project tiles (status pill, percent, progress bar, sparkline, 3-col footer) plus an 8th tile and a top-right ArrowUpRight CTA that both link to `/workspace/:id/projects`.

BL-WSUX-WSCTX-PERSIST.story: Workspace sidebar section shows up whenever the WorkspaceSwitcher has a workspace selected, not only on `/workspace/:id/*` routes. The wsId is resolved from the URL first, then falls back to the `useCurrentWorkspace` store on other views (dashboard, workspaces, admin). The section disappears only when no workspace is selected at all.

BL-PROJ-001.story: Project domain aggregate with ProjectId VO (UUID v7) and repository interface. Lifecycle: create / rename / changeSlug / changeDescription / softDelete / restore. Guards: name 1-120, slug kebab-case 1-120, description 0-500 (nullable). Foundation for the rest of the Projects module.

BL-PROJ-002.story: Public Projects module API — `ProjectsApi` (findById / findByWorkspace / findBySlug / exists), `ProjectView` DTO and integration events (ProjectCreated / Renamed / Updated / Deleted / Restored) consumed by Audit and future modules (Agents / Scheduler / Skills).

BL-PROJ-003.story: Doctrine XML mapping for Project aggregate + Postgres migration: new `projects` schema, `projects.projects` table, unique index `(workspace_id, slug) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`, FK to `workspaces.workspaces.id`. Custom `ProjectIdType`.

BL-PROJ-004.story: `CreateProject` command / handler + POST `/api/workspaces/{wsId}/projects` endpoint. Validates workspace membership, unique slug within workspace, returns 201 Created with `ProjectView`.

BL-PROJ-005.story: `ListProjectsByWorkspace` query / handler + GET `/api/workspaces/{wsId}/projects` endpoint. Every workspace member sees all workspace projects (per brief decision #1). Super admin sees everything.

BL-PROJ-006.story: `GetProject` query / handler + GET `/api/projects/{id}` endpoint. 404 for soft-deleted, 403 if user is not a member of the parent workspace.

BL-PROJ-007.story: `UpdateProject` command / handler (name / slug / description) + PUT `/api/projects/{id}` endpoint. Validates unique slug within workspace, 422 on collision, emits `ProjectUpdated` event with before/after.

BL-PROJ-008.story: `DeleteProject` command / handler (soft) + DELETE `/api/projects/{id}` endpoint. Also `RestoreProject` + POST `/api/projects/{id}/restore` for the Undoer. Events `ProjectDeleted` / `ProjectRestored`.

BL-PROJ-009.story: `ProjectsAuditListener` logs `project.create / rename / update / delete / restore` with before/after snapshot. `ProjectsUndoer` + `ProjectsUndoDescriber` enable reversible actions in Audit UI.

BL-PROJ-010.story: `WorkspaceDeletedListener` cascade soft-deletes all projects of the removed workspace (per brief decision #8). Workspace undoer also restores its projects.

BL-PROJ-011.story: Projects page (`/workspace/:wsId/projects`): `useProjects(wsId)` hook with React Query, `ProjectTile` component (name / slug / description preview / relative created_at), replaces the faux list in `ProjectOverviewsWidget` with real data. Empty state + loading skeleton.

BL-PROJ-012.story: “New project” modal (name required 1-120, slug auto-synced from name with live editing allowed, optional plaintext description 0-500). Client-side validation plus 422 handling from backend. After create, redirect to `/workspace/:wsId/project/:projId/overview`.

BL-PROJ-013.story: Project Overview page (`/workspace/:wsId/project/:projId/overview`) with routing `/workspace/:wsId/project/:projId` → redirect to overview. Breadcrumbs: Workspaces > {ws.name} > {project.name} > Overview. Shell with header (name + description) + placeholder for future widgets (BL-PROJ-OVERVIEW-* in upcoming milestones).

BL-PROJ-014.story: Context-aware Project sidebar section (shown only on `/workspace/:wsId/project/:projId/*`): active Overview + 7 disabled stubs (Agents / Members / Scheduler / Skills / Flow / Tasks / Settings) with a “Coming in X milestone” tooltip (per brief decisions #5 and #6).

BL-PROJ-015.story: Project Settings page (`/workspace/:wsId/project/:projId/settings`): edit form (name / slug / description) + Danger Zone section with Delete button (confirm modal, redirect to `/workspace/:wsId/projects` and toast linking to Undo via Audit).

BL-ORG-001.story: Organization aggregate with OrganizationId VO (UUID v7) + domain exceptions. Lifecycle: create / rename / changeSlug / softDelete / restore. Guards: name 1-100, slug kebab-case 1-120. 1:1 relation to owner (UserId) enforced at repository level.

BL-ORG-002.story: Public Organizations module API — `OrganizationsApi` (findById / findByOwner / findBySlug / exists), `OrganizationView` DTO and integration events (OrganizationCreated / Renamed / Deleted / Restored) for cross-module consumers.

BL-ORG-003.story: Doctrine XML mapping for Organization aggregate + Postgres migration: new `organizations` schema, `organizations.organizations` table, partial unique indexes on `(owner_user_id)` and `(slug)` WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, custom `OrganizationIdType`.

BL-ORG-004.story: `CreateOrganization` command / handler + POST `/api/organizations`. Auto-create on signup via `UserRegistered` event listener (name defaults to “{displayName}'s Organization”). Workspaces migration backfills `organization_id` column and indexes it.

BL-ORG-004b.story: Follow-up on workspace FK: make `workspaces.organization_id` NOT NULL + add FK constraint + wire `CreateWorkspaceCommand` to set the org from the acting user. Deferred — flagged in `questions-for-boss.md` (split vs monolith with BL-ORG-004).

BL-ORG-005.story: `UpdateOrganization` command / handler (partial name / slug) + PUT `/api/organizations/{id}`. Owner-only (403 for others), 404 for soft-deleted, slug uniqueness retried with random suffix on clash.

BL-ORG-006.story: `GetMyOrganizationQuery` + GET `/api/my/organization` returns the acting user's organization (null for invited users without an org). Powers sidebar OrgIdHeader and future owner-only gating.

BL-ORG-007.story: Organizations audit integration: `AuditLogger` wired into create / update handlers, `OrganizationsUndoer` + `OrganizationsUndoDescriber` enable Undo in Audit UI (Created → soft delete, Updated → restore previous name + slug).

BL-ORG-008.story: Sidebar refactor: top-level `OrgIdHeader` (short UUID + click-to-copy via `useMyOrganization()`), menu consolidated into one “General” section, Chat and Agents added as locked stubs, WorkspaceSwitcher trimmed (label + role pill removed).

BL-ORG-009.story: Organization Settings page (`/organization/settings`): edit form (name / slug with live-sync) + Danger Zone placeholder (delete deferred). Deferred to Phase 1 — not needed for MVP.

BL-ORG-010.story: Breadcrumbs owner / invited gating via `useMyOrganization()`: owners see `{OrgName} > {WorkspaceName} > ...`, invited users see `{WorkspaceName} > ...`. Deferred to Phase 1.

BL-PDOC-001.story: ProjectDoc aggregate with value objects (ProjectDocId / Slug / DisplayId) + DocType enum (ADR / Brief / Knowledge Base) + repository interface + ProjectDocsBundle skeleton.

BL-PDOC-002.story: ProjectDocsApi module interface + DocView DTO + integration events (DocCreated / Updated / Moved / Deleted / Restored) for cross-module consumers.

BL-PDOC-003.story: Doctrine XML mapping + migration for schema `project_docs` (table `docs`, partial UNIQUE on (project_id, doc_type, slug) and (project_id, doc_type, display_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, btree (project_id, doc_type) and (parent_doc_id)).

BL-PDOC-004.story: CreateDoc command/handler + POST `/api/projects/{projId}/docs` (auto `display_id` sequence per project per type + auto slug from title, doc_type required in payload).

BL-PDOC-005.story: ListDocsByProject query/handler + GET `/api/projects/{projId}/docs` (filter by doc_type and optional parent_doc_id, `?tree=1` returns nested tree for Knowledge Base).

BL-PDOC-006.story: GetDoc query/handler + GET `/api/docs/{id}` (resolve by UUID or by display_id via `/api/projects/{projId}/docs/{displayId}`).

BL-PDOC-007.story: UpdateDoc command/handler + PUT `/api/docs/{id}` (title / slug / content_markdown; slug uniqueness enforced per project+type; parent moves in BL-DOC-009).

BL-PDOC-008.story: DeleteDoc (soft) + DELETE `/api/docs/{id}` + RestoreDoc + POST `/api/docs/{id}/restore` (soft-delete orphans children: sets `parent_doc_id = NULL`).

BL-PDOC-009.story: MoveDoc command/handler (change parent_doc_id, same project only, cycle detection) + PATCH `/api/docs/{id}/parent`.

BL-PDOC-010.story: Audit integration: handlers log entries + ProjectDocsUndoer (Create/Update/Delete/Restore/Move) + ProjectDocsUndoDescriber EN/PL.

BL-PDOC-011.story: Cascade listener: `ProjectDeleted` → batch soft-delete all docs of the project + per-doc audit entry with `metadata.cascade.reason`.

BL-PDOC-012.story: Docs overview page `/workspace/:wsId/project/:projId/docs` (3 tiles: ADR count / Briefs count / KB count + CTAs) + `useDocsByProject` React Query hook + routing.

BL-PDOC-013.story: Typed list pages: `/docs/adr` (flat), `/docs/briefs` (flat), `/docs/knowledge-base` (tree sidebar + content pane) + DocTile + Create button.

BL-PDOC-014.story: Doc detail page `/docs/{type}/{displayId}` with markdown-it renderer + wiki-links `[[slug]]` plugin resolving to `<Link>` + children list (if parent) + edit button.

BL-PDOC-015.story: Doc editor page `/docs/{type}/{displayId}/edit` with form (title, slug override, parent_doc_id picker for KB, content textarea) + live preview split pane.

BL-PDOC-016.story: Doc delete flow (confirm dialog with acknowledge checkbox + redirect to list + inline success banner with Undo link to `/admin/audit`).

BL-PDOC-017.story: Unlock the Project sidebar **Docs** entry (disabled stub → active NavLink to `/docs`) + Project Overview page gets a “Latest docs” widget (top 5 recent docs).

BL-VAR-ARCH.story: Variables/secrets system — keys global + per workspace/project (IP_SERVERA, API_TOKEN). Agents reference via `$VAR_NAME` without exposing values in prompts. Needs brief.

BL-KB-ARCH.story: In-system knowledge base (not files) — shared level + dedicated per agent. Decisions: storage, retrieval, scope visibility. Needs brief.

BL-SKILL-ARCH.story: Skills system — atomic procedures per action (`new Symfony module`, `write SQL`, `verify branch`). Shared base + dedicated per agent. Needs brief.

BL-FLOW-ARCH.story: Flow Builder — agent orchestration in a project (Maja → brief → mockups → programming → CR → security) with optional approval gates. Core product feature. Needs brief.

BL-RUNTIME-STATES.story: Agent state machine — discovery/builder/analytics modes with auto-transitions (e.g., builder → listener when no work). Needs brief.

BL-RUNTIME-WORKERS.story: Worker split / thread orchestration — the agent (Viktor) branches work across isolated workers (worker-1/2/3); workers do not know about each other. Needs brief.

BL-RUNTIME-COMPACT.story: Context overflow safeguard — `is_first` flag + force-clear after context compact, agent rebuilds context from DB instead of using the compacted copy. Needs brief.

BL-RUNTIME-PROMPT-SYNC.story: Smart prompt sync — do not send the full prompt every time, the agent confirms it has up-to-date context, token savings. Needs brief.

BL-SCHED-ARCH.story: Cron-like scheduler for agents on workspace + project (e.g., daily content run in Agentic-Social-Media). Needs brief.

BL-DASH-ARCH.story: Page Builder for a project — widgets (roadmap, gantt, phases, metrics). Dedicated tabs per project. Ties into PLUGINS. Needs brief.

BL-AUTH-004.story: Short-lived access tokens (15 min) and an HttpOnly refresh cookie (14 d) that rotates on every refresh.

BL-AUTH-005.story: JTI denylist in Redis — forced revocation (logout-all, password change) invalidates sessions right away.

BL-CHAT-001.story: ChatSession aggregate + owner_user_id ACL + table chat.chat_sessions.

BL-CHAT-002.story: ChatThread aggregate (session FK + subject) + table chat.chat_threads.

BL-CHAT-003.story: ChatMessage aggregate with full envelope (17 fields, 6 enums) + table chat.chat_messages.

BL-CHAT-005.story: GET /api/chat/sessions/current — auto-create a session on first access.

BL-CHAT-006.story: GET /api/chat/sessions/{id}/threads — list threads owned by the actor.

BL-CHAT-F01.story: Frontend API layer — chat envelope types + four react-query hooks (session/threads/messages + sendMessage).

BL-CHAT-F02.story: /chat route + ChatPage shell: sidebar thread list + placeholder main panel.

BL-CHAT-F03.story: MessageList + MessageBubble — sender variants, priority badges, Intl timestamps.

BL-CHAT-F04.story: MessageComposer form (subject / priority / content / engine ID / engine type) submits via useSendMessage and resets on success.

BL-CAGU-001.story: chat_threads.parent_thread_id column + ChatThread attach/detach domain methods + repository findChildrenOf.

BL-CAGU-002.story: Stub table chat_thread_summaries with short_description + summary_json JSONB (filled later by CHAT-BRAIN).

BL-CAGU-003.story: GET /api/chat/agents/{id}/threads — list threads of one agent with aggregates (count, last message at).

BL-CAGU-004.story: POST /api/chat/threads — explicit thread creation with optional parentThreadId (same session).

BL-CAGU-005.story: POST /api/chat/threads/{id}/attach — attach a thread to a parent with cycle and cross-session guards.

BL-CAGU-006.story: POST /api/chat/threads/{id}/detach — detach a thread from its parent (no-op when already root).

BL-CAGU-006b.story: GET /api/chat/conversations — list user's agents with last-message preview and thread count (empty agents marked isNew).

BL-CAGU-007.story: Frontend API layer for agent-centric chat — types + four react-query hooks (useAgentConversations / useAgentThreads / useCreateThread / useAttachThread).

BL-CAGU-008.story: AgentsSidebar — left column lists agents with initials avatar, last message preview and a "new" badge for agents without history.

BL-CAGU-009a.story: Backend agents.agents.color field (nullable hex) + AgentColorPalette crc32 slug fallback — surfaced on AgentView, GET /api/agents and GET /api/chat/conversations.

BL-CAGU-009b.story: AgentsSidebar filtered to direct messages with a Direct Messages header, Add conversation button and per-agent avatar color.

BL-CAGU-009c.story: Add conversation modal with searchable agents table — clicking an agent creates a thread via useCreateThread and selects the agent.

BL-CAGU-010.story: ConversationFeed + ChatHeader + ThreadTabs — flat message feed per agent with an "All" chip, chapter dividers per thread and chips to filter to a single thread.

BL-CAGU-011.story: ThreadComposer — content textarea + Send + gear popover (engine type / engine id / priority / new-topic toggle with inline subject).

BL-CAGU-R.story: Chat redesign follow-up — dropped ThreadTabs + chapter dividers, flat chronological message stream per agent, per-agent color bubble tint, ChatSettingsModal moved to the header.

BL-AUTH-FP-001.story: Workers get a fingerprint — a stable hash of the host (machine id, mac, cpu) stored next to the worker. If the device changes, the backend notices.

BL-AUTH-JWT-001.story: Workers authenticate with JWT — short-lived access token (15 minutes) + refresh token (90 days) with one-use rotation, hashed in the database.

BL-WA-005a.story: Backend notices when a worker calls back with a different fingerprint — response flags a warning and keeps the previous fingerprint metadata.

BL-WA-005b.story: Fingerprint changes emit a domain event so other modules (audit, notifications) can react.

BL-WA-005c.story: Every fingerprint change is logged in the worker's history — detected and accepted entries side by side, kept in JSONB.

BL-WA-006a.story: You can accept a changed fingerprint via POST /api/workers/{id}/fingerprint/accept — the current hash rolls into the worker record.

BL-WA-007a.story: Worker daemon manages its own tokens — token manager + token exchange client call the refresh endpoint before the access token expires.

BL-WA-007c.story: Worker credentials file stores the refresh token alongside the pairing data (schema v2 on disk).

BL-WA-008a.story: Worker API client talks to the backend with Bearer JWT — on 401 it forces a refresh and retries the call once.

BL-WA-009a.story: WorkerAuthenticator prefers Bearer JWT via Lexik — legacy X-Worker-* header fallback is gated by a feature flag.

BL-WA-009b.story: Legacy X-Worker-* authentication is gone — along with the heartbeat endpoint and the secret token hash column.

BL-CAR-005b.story: Backend publishes AgentReplyRequested on RabbitMQ when a chat thread has a worker assigned — one message per reply request.

BL-CAR-005d.story: You can revoke a worker — single or all at once — and the backend cascades cleanup to assigned agents and chat sessions.

BL-CAR-006.story: Node worker daemon skeleton — TypeScript project with healthcheck server, structured logs and graceful shutdown on SIGTERM.

BL-CAR-007.story: Interactive pairing CLI — `pnpm pair` asks for the code, stores credentials to ~/.stellarcrew/worker.json with safe file permissions.

BL-CAR-008.story: Custom JSON serializer for AgentReplyRequested — worker consumes clean JSON, no PHP-specific metadata on the wire.

BL-CAR-008a.story: Worker AMQP consumer — binds a per-worker queue to the chat.agent_replies exchange and acks or requeues based on success.

BL-CAR-008b.story: Worker spawns `claude -p --resume` for each reply — captures stdout, trims, and records the reply back through the worker API.

BL-CAR-009.story: Mercure streams agent replies to the UI as Claude emits them — chunk-by-chunk instead of waiting for the final answer.

BL-CAR-010.story: Worker injects the agent's CLAUDE.md as a system prompt — Claude answers in the agent's voice, not plain default.

BL-WI-001.story: You generate a pairing code from the web panel — the response includes the one-line command to paste into your server.

BL-WI-002.story: GET /api/workers returns your workers — name, host, online/offline, last contact, fingerprint status.

BL-WI-003.story: Worker detail endpoint — full hardware info, fingerprint change history, and the list of agents assigned to this worker.

BL-WI-004.story: Workers store host info in JSONB — operating system, CPU, memory, kernel — populated from the worker on every token refresh.

BL-WI-005.story: Pair endpoint accepts host info — a freshly paired worker shows up with full hardware data from the start.

BL-WI-006.story: Token refresh exchange bumps the last-heartbeat timestamp and refreshes host info — the online badge reflects reality.

BL-WI-007.story: You can cancel a pairing code before it is used or expires.

BL-WI-008.story: A /settings/workers page lists your workers as cards — name, host, online dot, fingerprint status, hardware preview.

BL-WI-009.story: Every worker row has a kebab menu — Details, Copy ID, Revoke (with confirm).

BL-WI-010.story: Worker detail page — hardware, fingerprint with history + Accept button, and the agents assigned to this worker.

BL-WI-011.story: A banner over the workers list warns when any worker reports a device change — click through to accept or revoke.

BL-WI-012.story: The sidebar links to /settings/workers — you reach the list without typing the URL.

BL-WI-013.story: Frontend workers API layer — types + fetch functions + react-query hooks reused across the list, detail and modal.

BL-WI-014.story: Vitest and translations for /settings/workers — PL and EN side-by-side, all screens tested.

BL-WI-015.story: Add Worker modal — instance name, working directory, host description → one-line install command shown, modal waits until the worker pairs.

BL-WI-016.story: Copy-to-clipboard for the install command with a toast confirmation — plus a Regenerate button when the code expires.

BL-WI-017.story: A dedicated hook polls for the new worker to appear — it stops on success or when the code's time-to-live runs out.

BL-WI-018.story: Translations + Vitest for the Add Worker modal — PL/EN plus tests covering validation, polling, timeout and copy.

BL-WI-019.story: stellarcrew-worker CLI with subcommands — pair, start, status, logs, restart, unpair, list — each accepting an instance name.

BL-WI-020.story: Paths resolver for per-instance config and credentials — /etc/stellarcrew-worker/{instance}/ under root, ~/.stellarcrew/{instance}/ otherwise.

BL-WI-021.story: Systemd template unit stellarcrew-worker@.service — each instance runs as its own enabled service with logs via journalctl.

BL-WI-022.story: Worker builds as a single-file executable — one binary in /usr/local/bin/stellarcrew-worker, no node_modules on the server.

BL-WI-023.story: install-worker.sh — pulls the binary, installs the systemd unit, pairs with the code and starts the service in one shot.

BL-WI-024.story: Backend serves install-worker.sh — the panel generates copy-ready commands with the right base URL.

BL-WI-025.story: Worker CLI Vitest coverage + README section on installing in production — Manual install + CLI reference.

BL-DX-001.story: CI uses a ci/services block (postgres, redis, rabbit) instead of ad-hoc fakes — once tests move beyond the API surface.

BL-PDOC-001.story: Each merged milestone ships with a short user-facing release note in the PR body — changelog style, no internals.

BL-PDOC-002.story: Audit of stellarcrew.dev — compare copy, features and roadmap claims against v2 reality, list stale content and missing screenshots before touching the site.
